questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about The Plague is FALSE?

options.text: About one-third of the European population died.
It was later shown to be caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis.
It was spread directly from person to person with no animal involved.
The search for its cause helped spark the Renaissance.

questions.explanation: False. Fleas/rats spread the Plague; it was not simple personto-person spread.

questions.prompt: Fleas that spread the Plague picked up Yersinia pestis from:
questions.explanation: Rats.

questions.prompt: Explain how The Plague contributed to the birth of microbiology as a field.
questions.explanation: The mass, unexplained death drove people to seek a rational (rather than religious) explanation, which launched the Renaissance — considered the birth of modern science, and eventually microbiology.

questions.prompt: Who was the first person to observe microorganisms, and what did he call them?
questions.explanation: Anton van Leeuwenhoek; “animalcules.”

questions.prompt: What samples did Leeuwenhoek examine that led to the discovery of bacteria?
questions.explanation: Scrapings from between his own teeth, and later from the teeth of a man with rotting/decayed teeth.

questions.prompt: What is the size range of bacteria?
questions.explanation: 1–10 micrometers.

questions.prompt: Why did Leeuwenhoek’s discovery of bacteria in rotting teeth NOT lead him to conclude that bacteria cause disease?
questions.explanation: He observed more bacteria in rotting teeth than healthy teeth but reversed cause and effect — concluding that rotting teeth created the ideal environment for bacteria to spontaneously form, rather than that bacteria caused the rot.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the Germ Theory of Disease is FALSE?

options.text: Louis Pasteur first proposed that microbes could cause disease.
Robert Koch performed the experimental work that proved the theory.
The theory was established in the mid-to-late 1800s.
The theory was proposed and proven within the same decade.
It took roughly 200 years after bacteria were first observed for the theory to be established.

questions.explanation: False. Pasteur proposed the idea and Koch proved it, but this happened over time (mid-to-late 1800s), and roughly 200 years passed between the discovery of bacteria and the theory’s establishment.

questions.prompt: The Three Domain System classifies life based on:

options.text: Presence or absence of a cell wall

questions.explanation: Relatedness of nucleotide sequences.

questions.prompt: Name the three Domains of Life.
questions.explanation: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about prokaryotes and eukaryotes is FALSE?

options.text: Eukaryotes are generally larger (10–100 µm) than prokaryotes (1– 10 µm).
Bacteria and Archaea are both prokaryotes.

questions.explanation: False. Eukaryotes can be unicellular OR multicellular, not always multicellular.

questions.prompt: Which structural feature is unique to Bacteria and NOT shared by Archaea?
questions.explanation: Peptidoglycan cell wall (unique to Bacteria; Archaea have different wall chemistry).

questions.prompt: Describe one key similarity and one key difference between Bacteria and Archaea.
questions.explanation: Similarity: both are small, unicellular, prokaryotic. Difference: Bacteria have peptidoglycan cell walls and some cause disease; Archaea live in extreme environments and are not known to cause disease.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of a Domain Eukarya kingdom with its correct description is FALSE?

options.text: Protista — mostly unicellular, a highly diverse “miscellaneous” group
All four kingdoms belong to Domain Eukarya

questions.explanation: False. Fungi can be unicellular or multicellular, and they are heterotrophic (decomposers), not autotrophic.

questions.prompt: In the name Streptococcus pyogenes, the root “pyo” means:
questions.explanation: Pus.

questions.prompt: What is Binomial Classification, and give one example of what an organism’s name can reveal about it.
questions.explanation: Binomial Classification names organisms with a Latinized Genus + species (e.g., Streptococcus pyogenes). The root words can describe the organism — e.g., “strepto” (chain) + “coccus” (berry) describes its chain-of-berries appearance, and “pyo” (pus) + “gen” (formation) describes that it causes pus formation.

questions.prompt: Which statement about viruses, prions, and viroids is FALSE?

options.text: Viruses are non-living, obligate intracellular parasites.
Viruses are made of a protein capsid surrounding nucleic acid.
Prions are infectious proteins that contain their own nucleic acid.
Viroids are infectious pieces of RNA.
Viroids are only known to infect plants.

questions.explanation: False. Prions are infectious proteins with NO nucleic acid/genetic material at all.

questions.prompt: Which organism causes vaginitis?
questions.explanation: Candida albicans.

questions.prompt: Match each scientist to his key contribution: Robert Hooke, Anton van Leeuwenhoek, Louis Pasteur, Robert Koch.
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke — pioneered microscopy, published Micrographia, coined the term “cell.” Anton van Leeuwenhoek — first to observe bacteria/microorganisms (“animalcules”). Louis Pasteur — proposed microbes could cause disease. Robert Koch — provided the rigorous experimental proof of the Germ Theory of Disease.

questions.prompt: MRSA is an antibiotic-resistant strain of which organism?
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus.
